why: After sorting, the centres served by each warehouse form two contiguous groups, and one warehouse is best placed at its group's median. Prefix sums give each group's distance-to-median cost in O(1), so you try every split point. It sits in the 1-D DP week, but it is really a sorted split with prefix sums.
hints: With one warehouse on a line, where should it go to minimise the total distance? Then think about which centres each of two warehouses would serve.
Sort the positions. Each warehouse serves a contiguous block, so try every split into a left block and a right block; each block's best cost is the sum of distances to its median.
Prefix sums over the sorted array give a block's cost to its median in O(1): (median * left count - left sum) + (right sum - median * right count). O(n log n) for the sort plus O(n) for the splits.
pitfalls: With two or fewer centres the answer is 0.
Placing warehouses at the mean instead of the median gives the wrong total for absolute distances.
Forgetting to sort first breaks the 'contiguous groups' argument.
constraints:
• Bounds are not stated in the source. Reasonable: 1 <= n <= 10^5, 1 <= dist_centers[i] <= 10^9
  • Positions may repeat; the total may exceed 32 bits.
